clue.text: Group of days so far this month, notice

parts.note: the puzzle appeared in October, so this month is Oct, its usual abbreviation
an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: Someone tallies the days that have passed in the current month and posts a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle was published on 8 October 2003, so the days so far this month made a group of eight; 'this month' does double duty in the topical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An octad is a set of eight, and eight days had passed in the month on the day of publication.

clue.text: Commissioner and male chums from US entering sultan's territory

indicators.note: the male chums go into the territory

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate
buds is American slang for friends

explanation.surface: A commissioner and some American friends travel into a sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official commissioner appointed to investigate complaints.

clue.text: Sheep crossing river show spirit

indicators.note: the sheep straddle the river, so it sits inside

parts.note: tups are rams

explanation.surface: Flocks cross a stream showing pluck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests courage, but means a solvent here.
explanation.definitionFit: Turps, short for turpentine, is mineral spirit used as a solvent.

clue.text: Not so exciting, bumpy ride in the back? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: the surface says ride goes in the back, a container instruction
this reverses the stated arrangement, so the back goes in the ride instead
a bumpy ride is jolted about, signalling rearranging

parts.note: the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A jolting ride in the back seat is described as dull, though the opposite seems true.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the ride goes in the back; 'Quite the opposite' tells you to put the back inside the jumbled ride (DIER) instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearier is the comparative of dreary, meaning more dull and less exciting.

clue.text: Points made by people who may be poles apart

definitions.meaning: places on the earth's surface directly opposite one another

definitions.text: people who may be poles apart
definitions.meaning: inhabitants of the opposite side of the world, the word's original sense

explanation.surface: Arguments are put forward by people whose opinions are wildly opposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles apart' suggests disagreement, but it means living on opposite sides of the globe; 'made by' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodes are places diametrically opposite on the globe, and the word was once used for the people dwelling there.

clue.text: Top copy has wrong mark

parts.note: to ape is to copy
a cross marks an answer wrong

explanation.surface: A top-quality copy has a mistake marked on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip, the top.

clue.text: Mineral containing aluminium in pit discovered after journey

indicators.note: the mine part comes after the journey

parts.note: a tour is a journey

indicators.note: aluminium goes inside the pit

parts.note: a mine is a pit
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A mineral bearing aluminium is found in a mine after a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourmaline is a crystalline boron silicate mineral, often used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Mean attempt to hold up friend

indicators.note: in a down answer the attempt sits below the friend, supporting it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A stingy effort to rob a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' suggests robbery; in a down clue it means support from below.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means meagre or contemptibly small, as does mean.

clue.text: Strange twists with criminal perhaps involved in courageous action

indicators.note: the criminal is wrapped up within the strange word
twisting round turns the word back to front

parts.note: odd means strange
a criminal is one example of someone erring

explanation.surface: An odd turn of events with a crook mixed up in a brave deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange twists' reads as an odd turn of events, but it is a synonym turned back to front (DDO), split open by the criminal's activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring heroic action, the stuff of adventure stories.

clue.text: Second language, not half a racy one

indicators.note: not half keeps only the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A second tongue, but only part of a racy one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'language' earlier in the clue: a racy language.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, often racy language, so it is a racy kind of tongue.

clue.text: Boyfriend receives instruction in detailed memo

indicators.note: the boyfriend takes the instruction into himself, so it goes inside

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend
an order is an instruction

explanation.surface: A man's partner gets directions written up in a thorough note.
explanation.definitionFit: A bordereau is a detailed memorandum or schedule of documents, especially in insurance.

clue.text: Immature life form of particular value

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters from the following words, signalling a run hidden in them

explanation.surface: A young organism turns out to be of special worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature feeding stage of an insect before it changes into an adult.

clue.text: Some of the French having anger and lust

parts.note: des is the French partitive, meaning some of the
ire means anger

explanation.surface: A remark that the French are both hot-tempered and lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire as a noun is strong sexual longing, a synonym for lust.

clue.text: Carol, without place for shopping, is feeling the pain

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so carol wraps round the shopping place

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A carol singer far from the shops is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarting means suffering a sharp stinging pain, so it can replace feeling the pain.

clue.text: Just a dim friend in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A slow-witted friend is merely having difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as merely, but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair-minded means impartial and just in judgement.

clue.text: Label oriental furniture item as likely to sell

parts.note: to mark goods is to label them
E for East, oriental
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A dealer tags an Eastern piece of furniture as a good seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Marketable goods are ones that can be sold readily, so likely to sell fits.

clue.text: Has meal amid quarrels and yobbery.

indicators.note: the meal sits in the middle of the quarrels

parts.note: rows are quarrels
to dine is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Someone eats while fights and hooliganism rage around them.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is a British lout, so yobbery is loutish behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiness is noisy, disorderly behaviour, what yobs indulge in.

clue.text: Very eager to find a legendary giant

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, paired with Magog in British folklore

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled at the prospect of meeting a giant from legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes someone excited and eager to hear or see something.

clue.text: Express to go over viaduct, say

definitions.meaning: to cross a bridge such as a viaduct

explanation.surface: An express train passes over a viaduct.
explanation.definitionFit: To get across an idea is to express it, and to get across a viaduct is to cross it.

clue.text: Water creatures in a river fellow overlooks

indicators.note: in a down answer the fellow stands above the rest, looking over it

parts.note: a man is a fellow
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Aquatic animals in a river are watched by a man from above.
explanation.definitionFit: Manatees are large aquatic mammals, sea cows of warm coastal waters.

clue.text: Scientist taking leg off small creature

indicators.note: taking a thing off removes it, so the leg letters leave the scientist

parts.note: Isaac Newton, the physicist
on is the cricket term for the leg side of the field

explanation.surface: A scientist dissects a little animal by removing one of its legs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian, a little creature of ponds.

clue.text: Create British sporting arena and a suitable event for it

parts.note: a boxing ring is a sporting arena
a boxing bout takes place in a ring

explanation.surface: A promoter builds a British arena and stages a fight there.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about something is to cause it to happen, to create it.

clue.text: Old country spire's crumbling: answer?

indicators.note: a crumbling spire falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's is is: the spire is crumbling

explanation.surface: A church spire falling down poses a question about an ancient land.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia is the former name of Iran, an old country.

clue.text: Fantastic sound, strong but not hard

parts.note: a chime is a ringing sound

indicators.note: not hard means the hard letter is left out

parts.note: a rich flavour or colour is strong
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A noise is described as powerful though not harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimeric means imaginary or wildly fanciful, like a chimera, so fantastic in its unreal sense.

clue.text: Trophy I had obtained showing godlike figure

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A winner shows off the cup they won, featuring a statuette of a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman god of love, often shown as a winged figure.

clue.text: Host drinking sparkling wine and flavoured liquor

indicators.note: the host takes in the wine, so it goes inside

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a host
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: The party host downs some fizz and a flavoured spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is also a liquor flavoured with mastic resin, drunk in Greece and Turkey.

clue.text: A little time to get something cooked? Next to no time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
rice is something cooked

explanation.surface: A quick meal question: how long to cook something? Hardly any time.
explanation.definitionFit: A trice is an instant, a moment so short it is almost no time.

clue.text: News of whole area left out

indicators.note: left out means the left letter is removed

parts.note: the world is the whole area

explanation.surface: Reports from everywhere omit something.
explanation.definitionFit: Word can mean news or information, as in sending word.

clue.text: Produce record crowd

definitions.meaning: to make a vinyl disc by ... it
a crush of people, or to throng

explanation.surface: Turn out a disc that gathers a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl records are made by pressing, and a press is a dense crowd.

clue.text: Size of book producing bad mood — Euclid, putting learner off

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters are rearranged
putting the learner off removes that letter from the pool

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A book's format puts a reader in a bad mood, with Euclid shutting out the student.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange MOOD and EUCLID with L taken out ('putting learner off') to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Duodecimo is a book size made by folding sheets into twelve leaves.

clue.text: Dread being found out after record's scrapped

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the record

parts.note: a disc is a record; the 's is is

indicators.note: found out in the sense of thrown into disarray signals rearranging

explanation.surface: Fear on discovering that a recording has been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dread' looks like the start of the surface's story, but it is anagram fodder; 'being found out' jumbles it to ARDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded means thrown away, synonymous with scrapped.

clue.text: Saints held always to be wise men

indicators.note: the saints hold the word for always inside them

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for saints
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Saints have always been regarded as wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Seers are prophets, people credited with special wisdom and insight.
